description: Mainly an opening detector: fires right after the game's first stone when the opponent played it in column 6, 0, 1 or 3 (strongest for 6). Columns 2, 4 and 5 do not fire it. The other ~44% of firing is in mid-to-late boards with no clear tactical pattern. There the activation builds up over plies after one side's moves and is only weakly tied to last moves in column 6 or the top row.
effect: None measurable: setting it to max or to zero changes move probabilities by at most about 0.06 in 6 probe positions.
notes: Best dev F1 0.720 (P 1.00, R 0.563, AUROC 0.78) from the ply-1 rule. Adding top-row corner last moves dropped F1 to 0.476. Simulation share 0.03. Mid-game firing depends on the whole board: in a high board almost any last move fires, and activation alternates with parity and accumulates over plies. Vertical opponent pairs, threats and evaluation did not explain it. It may be a random direction whose cleanest response is the opening stone. A greedy synthesis reached 6.373, above the dev max of 6.241.
